lastRelease.name: v0.17.0
lastRelease.body:
### Added

- D(d,p)T proton transport in `nucleide-plasma-source` for deuterium-bearing
  ring/point and parametric sources (lattice stays rate-accounting-only):
  `Particle.species` (`Neutron` default, `Proton` additive),
  `SourceSampler::proton` and `ParametricProtonSampler` as independent
  seeded instances (zero new draws on any neutron path), the Brysk-Gaussian
  proton line (`reaction::proton_moments_mev`, `SpectrumSpec::from_proton`;
  `E0 = 3.02` MeV, `sigma = sqrt(1.51·Ti [MeV])`; `Ti = 20` keV → 3.02 MeV,
  `0.173782` MeV), and MCNP6-only `PAR=h` SDEF cards
  (`emit_sdef_proton` / `emit_sdef_parametric_proton`) with a `proton branch`
  drift row. The proton rate is the D-D neutron-branch rate reused
  bit-for-bit (50/50; flat-profile anchors `P = 13012914793.607618`
  pure D-D and `P = 6376328248.867733` for 70/30). D-T-only proton
  requests, MCNP5 proton cards, and lattice proton transport stay loud;
  there are no Serpent proton cards (its `PART='p'` means photons), so the
  Python/WASM facades return `serpent: None` for proton specs. Python gains
  the optional `species` spec key, the `species` particle array,
  `proton_moments()`, and a `mcnp_version=6` requirement for proton cards;
  WASM gains `fusionProtonMoments()`, `species` on fusion sample/card
  specs, and per-particle `species`. The interactive fusion demo's lattice
  panel now exposes the species-temperature pair.

- Optional separate D(d,p) proton-rate model in `nucleide-plasma-source`:
  parametric specs take `proton_rate_model="bosch_hale_ddp"` (Python key;
  WASM `protonRateModel`) to use the published Bosch–Hale D(d,p) Table VII
  fit instead of the pinned 50/50 accounting anchor. The default
  `"pinned_50_50"` stays bit-for-bit; the opt-in branch ratio is `0.9218`
  at 20 keV (7.8% below the D(d,n) branch), so `proton_per_neutron` for
  pure D-D becomes that physical share. The proton line shape, sampler
  draw accounting, and card syntax are unchanged; `proton_accounting`
  reports the selected `proton_rate_model`, and the `proton branch` drift
  row names it. Ring/point and lattice accounting keep the pinned
  convention.

- End-to-end first-wall workflow (tutorial
  `docs/tutorials/python/fusion-first-wall.md` and notebook
  `notebooks/first-wall-workflow.ipynb`): screening-level chain from a
  synthetic parametric D-T source and caller wall-load flux through CSG
  translation, weight windows, MCPL exchange, R2S/ALARA/FISPACT parsing,
  one-full-power-year damage with uncertainty, clearance screening over the
  parsed inventory, tritium permeation scoping, and a SAND-II foil check.
  Every number is synthetic, the wall load defaults to 1.5 MW/m² with a
  caller override, and both the tutorial and the notebook execute in CI.

- FESTIM parity probe `validation/tritium_vs_festim.py`: a black-box
  comparison of the 1D tritium kernel against FESTIM 2.1 (`festim==2.1`,
  Apache-2.0, v2.x API) over trap-free, one-trap, Sieverts, and two-layer
  legs with manufactured-solution and analytic-permeation self-gates.
  The probe runs only in the probe-only `dolfinx/dolfinx:stable` image
  (docker route, documented in `validation/README.md`) and SKIPs loudly
  with its reason everywhere else; FESTIM never enters the main
  validation container or the Rust workspace. Committed `results.md`
  numbers regenerate only from a probe-image run.

- Per-species ion temperatures on single-fuel lattice configs in
  `nucleide-plasma-source` (the 0.16 parametric solo convention ported to
  `LatticeSourceConfig`): single-fuel D-T reacts at the mass-weighted
  `T_DT = T_D + (2/5)·(T_T − T_D)`, single-fuel D-D at `T_D`, with the
  Ballabio lines following per branch (D-T at `T_DT`, D-D at `T_D`). Equal
  pair temperatures `(T, T)` reproduce the shared-temperature single-fuel
  lattice kernel bit-for-bit (strengths, sampled stream, cards). Anchors:
  `(T_D, T_T) = (20, 30)` keV gives `T_DT = 24` keV with the D-T line at mean
  14.077934372230146 MeV, sigma 0.3700390508551786 MeV. Mixture paths are
  untouched; the `None`-pair path keeps the landed expression trees verbatim
  (no new RNG draws); the per-node tail spelling stays out of scope.

- Deuterium hot-tail fraction on lattice configs in `nucleide-plasma-source`
  (the parametric `DeuteriumTail` rule ported per node): `LatticeSourceConfig`
  gains an optional `tail` mirroring `ParametricPlasmaConfig::tail` — one
  global `(η, T_tail)` applied at every node with the node temperature as
  the bulk `T_D`, reacting the five bulk/tail sub-branches (D-T at
  `T_DT`/`T_DTt`, D-D at `T_D`/`T_mix`/`T_tail`) through the same per-particle
  branch roulette, card energy marginals, and `deuterium tail` drift row
  (rate-weighted tail share). Anchors: the 70/30 blend at `(T_D, T_T) =
  (20, 30)` keV with `η = 0.05` at `T_tail = 60` keV gives `S =
  1177836136801.1577` at `n = 1e20` m⁻³ (reconstructed from the per-node
  branch weights) with the five Ballabio lines at 24/48/20/40/60 keV;
  `η = 0` reproduces the no-tail lattice kernel bit-for-bit (any `T_tail`),
  and a tail without a fuel mixture is loud. Python gains the
  `deuterium_tail` dict on lattice specs; WASM `sampleLatticeSource`
  gains the `fuelDeuterium`/`fuelTritium` mixture pair plus
  `tailFraction`/`tailTempKev` (both-or-neither loud, needs the mixture).

- Python tutorial "Solve activation with ACTINV"
  (`docs/tutorials/python/solve-with-actinv.md`): maps one material, one
  spectrum, and one schedule from the Nucleide ALARA/R2S surfaces to an
  `actinv-spec-1` problem, solves with the optional ACTINV CLI (pinned
  `actinv==1.4.0`, data catalog `1.1.0` with the recorded library hash),
  and reads the photon source back with Nucleide's existing
  `.photonSrc` readers. Docs only — no Nucleide dependency on ACTINV,
  no vendored code or data; the example files stay in the ACTINV
  repository. Carries the research-grade qualification, the TENDL-2025
  data defects, and the TOTAL-only photon limit.

- Adaptive per-sample bandwidths for Gaussian KDE source sampling in
  `nucleide-vr-tools`: `Bandwidth::AdaptiveKnn { k, scale }` (a synthetic
  KDSource-class case) gives each fitted sample its own width
  `h_i0 = scale · dist_k(x_i)` in σ-scaled coordinates with
  `h_ij = h_i0 · σ_j`, so tight clusters smooth lightly and sparse tails
  smooth broadly. `dist_k` is the 1-based leave-one-out `k`-th nearest
  neighbour (`1 <= k <= n - 1`); `pdf` normalizes per sample and `draw`
  perturbs the centre with its own width row, keeping the deterministic
  caller-random style. Invalid rank/scale, duplicate points (zero
  distance), and zero-variance dims are loud errors — a zero bandwidth is
  never a delta spike. Python: `KdeSampler(rows, "adaptive", k=k,
  scale=scale)` plus `sample_bandwidths()`. Hand vector: `{0, 0.2, 0.4,
  10}` with `k = 1` gives widths `0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 9.6` and
  `pdf(0) = 0.8746688805236177`.

- Interactive demo parity (0.17.0): the variance-reduction demo gains a
  KDE section (Silverman/fixed/adaptive rule selector, synthetic
  `{0, 0.2, 0.4, 10}` default rows, fitted bandwidths, density curve,
  and a deterministic draw; WASM `kdeFit`/`kdePdf`/`kdeDraw`/
  `kdeSampleBandwidths` mirroring the Python kwargs), the fusion demo's
  lattice tab gains the fuel/tail inputs blank by default, the
  parametric tab gains a Neutron/Proton selector with D(d,p)T proton
  moments, and the tritium tutorial notes the FESTIM 2.1 parity
  (F1–F4 PASS over `J_ss`/`J(t)`/`t_lag`/`c(x)`).

lastRelease.name: v0.3.0
lastRelease.body:
NukeIDE 0.3.0 unifies NukeAI behind one capability catalog, extends safe OpenMC edits to project metadata, advanced settings, and fixed-source sources, adds a parametric CAD component library, and completes a theme-and-accessibility pass across empty states, action menus, and viewers.

### Added

- nuke-ai: safe edits preview and apply OpenMC project name, description, and author changes with confirmation and session-scoped undo.
- openmc-studio: NukeAI reads the run mode and every supported OpenMC settings value before previewing an edit.
- openmc-studio: NukeAI advanced settings edits cover output, particle cutoffs, and kinetics (IFP) with nested-safe undo and IFP/inactive cross-checks.
- openmc-studio: NukeAI previews, applies, and undoes independent OpenMC source add/update/remove edits for fixed-source runs, with a read-only source inventory.
- nuke-cad: parametric components add box, cylinder, tube, sphere, cone, and plate-with-hole templates with editable dimensions and radius/diameter aliases.
- nuke-cad: mechanical component templates add L bracket, flange, stepped shaft, pipe with bore, and bolt-circle plate starters.
- nuke-cad: nuclear component templates add hex cell, control-rod guide tube, and assembly grid plate starters.
- nuke-essentials: a shared compact action menu supports host icons, icon-only triggers, keyboard navigation, focus return, and top/bottom placement.
- nuke-ai: embedded action menus make the read-only context actions visible in the statepoint loader, CAD search launcher, and DAGMC editor.
- nuke-visualizer: the statepoint viewer header and empty loader expose Ask About Context, Explain Statepoint, and Diagnose Statepoint.
- openmc-studio: the DAGMC editor header exposes NukeAI actions while the Simulation tab keeps its validation and run groups.

### Changed

- nuke-ai: the chat prompt, chat tool list, Diagnostics tool list, skill allowlists, and MCP read-only allowlist are generated from one capability catalog, so enabled capabilities cannot silently disappear.
- nuke-cad: component-template count parameters rebuild the requested pattern or hole array at creation time instead of staying at the shipped count.
- nuke-cad: NukeAI actions move beside the floating CAD search launcher and open upward, keeping the ribbon uncluttered and the menu clear of dialogs.
- nuke-cad: Feature Tree uses an indented tree-list glyph, distinct from OpenMC Geometry's cell hierarchy.
- nuke-cad: BOM, Model Outline, and Feature Tree empty states use the shared card, drop duplicate status rows, and offer New CAD Document/Open CAD Viewport actions.
- nuke-visualizer: CSG/DAGMC outlines, Dataset Inspector, and Viewer Settings use the shared empty-state card; OpenMC geometry/tally cards align at the top.
- nuke-visualizer: CSG Outline uses one overlapping-primitives glyph in its empty card, sidebar/tab icon, and Nuke Tools entry, keeping it distinct from OpenMC Geometry.
- nuke-visualizer: OpenMC Geometry uses the same cell-node glyph in its tab, Nuke Tools entry, and empty card.
- nuke-ai: Diagnose CSG Geometry uses the shared CSG primitives glyph instead of the old symbol icon.
- nuke-essentials: the generic code Outline view is closed in the default shell; reopen it from View → Outline for code files.

### Fixed

- nuke-cad: the Appearance opacity field uses the themed input chrome instead of a white native number field, and opacity-only edits keep the theme body color.
- nuke-cad: the duplicate unsaved dot behind the document toolbar is removed; the toolbar's own dot is the single indicator.
- nuke-essentials: the Welcome page scrolls vertically when walkthroughs and recent workspaces exceed the viewport.
- nuke-essentials: recent-workspace rows keep a flat hover surface instead of underlining the path.
- nuke-essentials: illustrated empty-state icons and CAD mask glyphs render at the intended size instead of Theia's 16px codicon default.
- nuke-essentials: shared dialogs, color picker, viewer bar, ViewCube, and view badges expose screen-reader names and keyboard-focus tooltips.
- nuke-ai: NukeAI action menus use an icon-only bot trigger with a tooltip, and dashboard groups use the bot icon and sentence-case labels.
- nuke-ai: detached chat windows keep the NukeAI welcome and tool-card styling.
- openmc-studio: tally and dashboard checkboxes follow the active theme, checkbox labels stay sentence case, and icon-only actions expose screen-reader names.
- nuke-visualizer: probe and find-data cards share one slot without covering each other or the bottom bar, the viewer bar wraps on narrow panels, and icon-only controls expose screen-reader names.

lastRelease.name: v2.1.0
lastRelease.body:
### Added

- Pull-based production deploys: pin `NUKELAB_VERSION` or `NUKELAB_IMAGE_TAG`
  to switch `nukelabctl up` / `update` from source builds to pulling tagged
  `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend` and `-frontend` images. The three
  backend services share one backend image; `update --build` forces a source
  rebuild even in pull mode. Unpinned deploys keep today's source-build
  behavior.
- Release versioning: git tags (`vX.Y.Z`) are the single source of truth.
  `scripts/bump-version.sh` syncs the version across `VERSION`,
  `backend/app/version.py`, `frontend/package.json`, and this changelog.
- Dynamic version injection: CI image builds pass the resolved tag as the
  `APP_VERSION` build arg (`backend/Dockerfile`), so running containers
  report the exact image tag (`2.1.0`, `main`, `pr-42`). The API root,
  `/health/status`, and the OpenTelemetry service version resolve via
  `settings.app_version`; empty or unset `APP_VERSION` falls back to the
  static literal in `app/version.py`.
- Compose builds bake the platform version into locally built backend images:
  `nukelabctl` exports `NUKELAB_VERSION` (from the `VERSION` file / git tag,
  overridable via the env file) and `compose.yml` passes it as the
  `APP_VERSION` build arg to the backend and celery images, so stacks
  deployed with `nukelabctl` report the checkout version instead of
  `0.0.0-dev`.
- Automatic pre-migration backups: `./nukelabctl db-migrate` now takes a
  `pg_dump` snapshot before running `alembic upgrade head`. The snapshot name
  is `backups/pre-migrate-<NUKELAB_VERSION>-<current-revision>-<timestamp>.dump`.
  If the backup fails, the migration aborts; if the migration then fails, the
  exact `./nukelabctl restore <file>` command is printed. Use `--no-backup` to
  skip the snapshot.
- Startup schema-compatibility guard (`app/db/schema_guard.py`) refuses to boot
  an old backend image against a newer database schema. Controlled by the
  `DB_SCHEMA_GUARD` setting (`auto` refuse in production/warn elsewhere,
  `enforce` always refuse, `off` disabled). If the database is unreachable the
  guard logs a warning and does not block startup.
- Environment-file drift detection and repair: `./nukelabctl check-env` compares
  `.env` / `.env.development` against `.env.example` and reports missing or
  stale keys (optionally value differences with `--changed`, all files with
  `--all`). `./nukelabctl sync-env` non-destructively appends missing keys from
  `.env.example` while preserving existing local values and secrets; stale keys
  are reported but left for manual removal. Both commands are read-only by
  default unless `sync-env` is invoked with `--yes` or confirmed interactively.
- Production version guard: when `APP_ENV=production`, `nukelabctl` refuses to
  boot if the resolved version is `0.0.0-dev`. Production requires a real
  release via `VERSION`, a git tag, or an explicit `NUKELAB_VERSION` /
  `NUKELAB_IMAGE_TAG` (the latter is useful when pulling pre-built GHCR
  images).

### Changed

- Backend version string is no longer hardcoded: `app/main.py`,
  `app/api/health.py`, and the OpenTelemetry service version in
  `app/config.py` all resolve through `settings.app_version` (env-first,
  static fallback in `app/version.py`).
- The static fallback in `app/version.py` is now the fixed sentinel
  `0.0.0-dev` instead of a release-looking literal — a version that can
  never be mistaken for a release, and which `bump-version.sh` no longer
  touches (only `VERSION`, `frontend/package.json` + lockfile, and this
  changelog are bumped at release time).
- `frontend/package.json` version set from `0.0.0` placeholder to the
  platform version.

### Fixed

- CI/CD workflow now triggers on `v*.*.*` tags and builds/pushes release
  images when a tag is pushed, including platform environment images
  (`nukelab-environment-base`, `nukelab-environment-conda-base`, `nukelab-environment-workspace`, `nukelab-environment-dev`).
  The `build-images` job and per-matrix `Build and push` step both run for tag
  pushes regardless of path-filter results, and the path-filter `any` rule is
  updated so version-only changes trigger builds. A new `Release` workflow
  creates a draft GitHub Release from the matching `CHANGELOG.md` section and
  appends the published container image references.


## Container images

| Image | Tag |
|-------|-----|
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend` | `2.1.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-frontend` | `2.1.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-auth-sidecar` | `2.1.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-base` | `2.1.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-conda-base` | `2.1.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-workspace` | `2.1.0` |
| `ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-dev` | `2.1.0` |

All images are also tagged as `latest`.

### Pull all images

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-backend:2.1.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-frontend:2.1.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-auth-sidecar:2.1.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-base:2.1.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-conda-base:2.1.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-workspace:2.1.0
docker pull ghcr.io/nukehub-dev/nukelab-environment-dev:2.1.0
```
